jobs.title: Last call
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 27, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Friday. Last call through the wall. The bar's lights going off, drawn as the plaster going dark. Then one sound: the back door. Then the alley: one regular, from behind, walking home past the garage. The only one the strip ever draws outside the wall. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a garage wall where figures drawn in the plaster are fading as a bar closes behind it, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a dark plaster wall with one small rectangle of light where a door opens and closes, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, seen through a garage window, a man in a hat walking slowly away down an alley at night, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a man and a dog at a garage window looking at an empty alley beside a dark tavern, no words (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_garage shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31; @loc_garage for the setting.
